First Semester Lecture Timetable

All levels · Mon–Thu 7 am–5 pm (break 1–2 pm) · Fri 7 am–1 pm

QUICK INFORMATION
Students

Tap your level or choose a lecturer (or click any lecturer's name) to see just that schedule. Tap a class for details. Your choice is remembered on this device.

    Each 3-unit course meets for 2 hours on one day and 1 hour on another day, in the same venue. Classes start from 7 am; only Professors have no 7 am lectures, and 1-hour classes never start at 7 or 8 am. There are no lectures on Wednesday 9–10 am (Chapel Seminar). A course's level comes from its code (ECON 1xx is 100 Level, ECON 2xx is 200 Level, and so on). Service courses for other departments keep the times those departments set. No lecturer, venue or class of students has two lectures at the same time, and no departmental lecture holds during the Thursday 11 am–1 pm Departmental Seminar. GST, GEDS, ENT, SSC and ACC courses are shown so students can see their full day. Comments: Departmental Planning Committee.

    Add to calendar

    Creates a calendar file (.ics) with every class repeating weekly, a reminder at 7 pm the evening before (so 7 am starts are never missed) and another 15 minutes before each lecture. Open it on your phone or import it into Google Calendar or Outlook. Times are West Africa Time.

    Find a free room

    Green rooms are free for that hour. Online and studio rooms are not listed.

    Download the timetable

    Notifications

    Reminders for lecturers and change alerts for lecturers and students. Email addresses you enter stay on this device only; they are not published with the timetable.

    What changed

    To show the change on this page for everyone, staff with edit access can use "Edit timetable", which also lists it under "What has changed". With automatic emails turned on, adding the same change to the Changes sheet emails everyone automatically.

    Lecturers

    Type each lecturer's email, or upload a CSV file with two columns: Name, Email.

    Students

    Upload a CSV file with columns: Email, Level (100, 200, 300, 400 or Service). You can also paste the list below, one student per line.

    A web page cannot send emails by itself, so for fully automatic emails use this free Google Sheets kit. Once set up, it runs on its own from the department's Google account:

    • Lecturers: every evening (6 pm by default) each lecturer teaching the next day gets their lectures, with 7 am starts flagged "Early start". Optionally, a "starting soon" email before each lecture.
    • Students: every evening, the next day's classes for their level (sent in BCC). Optionally, a "starting soon" email too.
    • On or off: lecturer and student reminders can each be switched on or off on the Settings sheet or from the "Timetable alerts" menu.
    • Changes: when you log a change on the Changes sheet, the lecturer and, if you choose, the students of that level are emailed within an hour.

    The Google Sheet is made from the timetable as it is right now, and includes any lecturer and student emails saved on this device.

    Setup takes about 10 minutes and is explained on the first sheet. Everyone can also get phone reminders without any setup by using "Add to calendar".

    The current timetable, , will be kept under 🕘 Versions & semesters, where anyone can still open it.

    The new timetable starts empty: no courses, and no lecturers or venues assigned. You then enter the department's course allocation (which lecturer takes which course), and Generate sets the days, times and venues.

    Options (what to keep)
